record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: In the quantitative-logic framework where meta-degrees are obtained by aggregating formula truth degrees across valuations, is a measure on the truth-degree set genuinely necessary, as it is in the integral-based case, or can a satisfactory theory be developed without introducing a measure?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2 (S. Gottwald). Particularly, does one need – as in the case of the integral – a measure in the truth degree set, or can one do well without, too?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let L be a (truth-degree) set, typically a subset of the unit interval [0,1] equipped with the operations of a residuated lattice or t-norm-based structure, that serves as the codomain of truth-value evaluations of formulas of a fuzzy propositional logic. Given a non-empty class V of valuations v : Form → L, the truth degree of a formula φ under v is v(φ) ∈ L. A meta-degree of φ is obtained by aggregating the family {v(φ) : v ∈ V} into a single value in [0,1]; one classical way to do this is to integrate the function v ↦ v(φ) with respect to some measure on V (or, after pushforward, with respect to a measure on the truth-degree set L), yielding an integral-based theory of degrees of truth/validity.

Question: In the quantitative-logic framework where meta-degrees are produced by aggregating the truth degrees v(φ) of a formula φ across valuations v ∈ V, is the introduction of a measure (on the valuation space, or equivalently on the truth-degree set L) genuinely indispensable for developing a satisfactory theory of meta-degrees—as it is in the integral-based approach—or can a coherent and adequately expressive theory of such meta-degrees be constructed without ever introducing a measure?
artifact.status_search_result: No clear resolution of this question was located in the available literature on quantitative fuzzy logic and meta-degrees; the problem appears to remain in the status of an open conceptual problem posed in the fuzzy logic community, but verification of a definitive answer could not be obtained.
